newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast prods ease despite late NYMEX rebound - May 14.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast prods ease despite late NYMEX rebound - May 14.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined product prices were mostly lower Wednesday, tracking lower NYMEX energy prices amid ample supplies, traders said.
On the NYMEX, June crude oil shed 0.38 cents a barrel to 64.38 a barrel, while heating oil eased 0.06 cents a gallon to 56.42 cents a gallon.
A sharp rebound in futures failed to totally erase early session weakness, which sidelined buyers.
Ample supplies also weakened prices, with trade group American Petroleum Institute (API) reporting late Tuesday that West Coast gasoline stocks rose a 1.8 million barrels last week to 30.4 million.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged May shipments of CARB gasoline at 61.50/62.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, down a cent from Tuesday.
But conventional grade unleaded increased a half cent to 60/61 cents, as buyers stepped up to take deliveries after NYMEX crude oil made slight gains on short covering.
++ DISTILLATES: May CARB diesel fuel dropped one cent a gallon in Los Angeles to 60/61 cents, while jet fuel fell 0.50 cents to 60/61 as well.
